results.evidence: [logged ac-refuter return, repaired before this record] The check runs on value.strip(), so a record_id with a leading or trailing control character is accepted, not rejected. I called _record_id directly. It returned 'abc' for 'abc\n', 'abc\x85' (U+0085), '\x1fabc' and 'abc\t', and it returned None for the 65-char id, 'a@b' and 'a\x7f'. The AC says a record_id that 'contains ... a control character' is rejected. The code accepts any of these ids and stores the stripped value. The 65-char, '@' and inner or DEL cases do reject. I did not run the CLI import or read the import_rejected payloads from sqlite. I also did not check whether an earlier-ordered schema error reports its own field instead of record_id.

tests/test_prospects_record_id_terminal.py passed (15/15). Real CLI reproduction (migrate, then prospects-import, with COTTONWOOD_CONFIG set and temp dirs only) was run for 8 ids: 65 'a' characters, 'pat@acme', an inner ESC, a trailing '\n', a leading '\t', a trailing U+0085, DEL, and a leading U+001F. Every import exited 1 with stderr 'rejected record 1: record_id: record-id'. Each import_rejected payload read from sqlite had field='record_id', rule='record-id' and record_id=null. None of the payloads contained the offending value. validate.py:358 defines the pattern [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}. Line 369 applies it with fullmatch after trimming spaces only. Line 440 yields ('record_id',) when the id is invalid.

The new pattern [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} fully matches 'acme-1.v2_x', so the record is not rejected. A real CLI run (main prospects-import, migrated temp db, temp yaml config with backup_dir) printed 'record 1 (acme-1.v2_x): created lead 1 (direct_candidate)' and 'imported 1, matched 0, rejected 0', with exit code 0. tests/test_prospects_record_id_terminal.py passed 9/9, including test_a_plain_record_id_imports_and_is_printed, which asserts that exact output.

I imported a record with organization.category 'dental' through the real CLI (uv run cottonwood prospects-import) into a temp DB. I then re-imported it with the category 'ortho\u001b[31mdontics', written with json.dump. The difference line printed was: "record 1 (acme-1): organization.category differs: stored 'dental', incoming 'ortho[31mdontics' (kept stored)". Checked as bytes, there was no 0x1b in stdout or stderr; the check printed False. tests/test_prospects_record_id_terminal.py passed (9 passed). The test at line 135 covers the same case. Difference values go through terminal.printable at cottonwood/prospects.py:431, and printable drops Unicode Cc and Cf characters.
